test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 11 Oct 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All Bats are Mammals.

Some Bats are Viruses.

All Viruses are Diseases.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some Bats are Diseases.

(II) Some Mammals are Viruses.
solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f68900380fd3c316ed2ac973dd5765187c30396b815327397fef453422bc7176.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some Bats are Diseases → **F**ollow (As some Bats are Viruses and all Viruses are Diseases. As some part of bats is common with viruses which whole comes in diseases, therefore it is true.)

(II) Some Mammals are Viruses → Follow (As all Bats are Mammals and some Bats are Viruses. As whole bats comes in mammals and has some part common with viruses, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Both conclusions (I) and (II) follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
